text:
alice: :rotating_light: noticing spike on prod-inferers-6 memory, visible KV cache growth after a deploy. Streaming requests start dropping tokens mid-stream.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-032 (kv-cache + streaming partial flush). Paging on-call: @raj

raj: I'm on it. Paging logs + quick assessment now. Which region?

alice: eu-west-1 primarily, but a subset in us-west-2. Error rates up for streaming endpoints with continuous-batching enabled.

maria: Observed long tail of `batch_wait_ms` and token cadence stalls. Samples show incomplete chunks, clients see "..." and then stream ends.

ben: Dumped meminfo on one worker:
``
PID  1234  VmRSS: 14.3G  kv_cache_entries: 2.1M  batch_queue_len: 67
ERROR repeated: kv_cache_grow: eviction stalled
```

raj: Looks like kv-cache blowup plus batch merging keeps delaying flush. Two mitigations: 1) disable continuous batching on the fleet 2) force KV eviction/trim. Which to prefer for fastest mitigation?

josh: I'd do (1) first — reduce risk of partial flushes immediately. Then (2) as follow-up. Disabling continuous batching is a config flip via runtime API.

maria: Agreed. Patch ready: set `continuous_batching.enabled=false` and reduce `batch_max_tokens` from 2048->512 for streaming pool.

raj: Applying hotfix to eu-west-1 now. Command:
``
curl -XPOST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/runtime/flip -d '{"pool":"streaming-eu","continuous_batching.enabled":false,"batch_max_tokens":512}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP"
```

sre-bot: Deploy change rolled to 60% in eu-west-1 via canary.

alice: After flip: memory on nodes dropping, request latencies improved, streaming completes end-to-end but still some partial chunks for a few in-flight sessions.

raj: For in-flight sessions we can't reconstruct. Noting affected customers: partner_acme, quickchat.ai. Customer success pinged.

ben: Running `kv_cache.trim(aggressiveness=2)` on the cluster to reclaim space.

josh: Trim complete. Logs show eviction completed across streamers.

maria: Following trim, observed that new streams are stable. Regen rate for token cadence normalized.

raj: Confirming: error rate for streaming endpoints down from 4.8% -> 0.6% in last 15m. Throughput back to normal for dedicated pools.

alice: Root cause hypothesis: a recent change in the approximate-KV sizing logic + a corner case in continuous-batching merge allowed cache to grow beyond eviction triggers. That made batch flush latencies spike -> streaming token_timer didn't fire predictably -> partial flush bug surface.

maria: Created a short-term patch for token flush: ensure `force_flush_on_timer=true` when continuous batching enabled. Will PR to mainline after incident.

raj: On-call handoff: @raj handing to @ben for 18:00-02:00 UTC. Ben will own follow-up and customer comms.

ben: Taking over. Action items: 1) stabilize rolling config to disable continuous batching for streaming-critical pools 2) run eviction audits 3) coordinate postmortem and customer impact matrix.

sre-bot: Noted handoff in incident tracker. Created follow-up ticket: INFRA-1894 (kv-cache regen + continuous-batching safe defaults)

alice: Customer success update: acme reported 6 partial responses in last hour; offered immediate apologize + temporary dedicated pool. CS will follow up with credits.

josh: Postmortem checklist: attach logs, ddtrace segments, batching histograms, kv cache size timeline, and the quickfix commands used.

maria: Will start drafting the postmortem. Tagging @product for visibility on rolling disable of continuous batching for streaming features.

raj: Leaving notes in thread. If anything regresses, @pagerduty-bot will escalate to SRE lead.

ben: Closing active mitigation. Will schedule a rollback test and a patch to KV sizing logic and continuous-batching merge sequence. Thanks all.

sre-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident timeline: start=1772456789 mitigated=1772460389

alice: Great work everyone :tada:
